study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Martin et al., Drug and Alcohol Dependence Reports, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Sex differences in normative modeling of cortical thickness in cannabis use disorder

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states it will examine sex differences in brain regions using normative modeling-derived z-scores in adults with CUD and test associations with behavioral variables, specifying reliance on a large normative reference population.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "The aim of the present study was to examine sex differences in brain regions using measures derived from normative modeling... We therefore tested for differences in normed z-scores between males and females with CUD using baseline data from two clinical trials. Of regions that demonstrated a sex difference, we examined whether these z-scores correlated with relevant behavioral variables..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: An EXISTING normative model (NOMIS) was used. The paper cites the original publications and specifies the normative sample size (n=6909 healthy adults) and variables modeled. However, detailed eligibility criteria, image quality standards, and exclusion reasons for the normative reference cohort are not described in this paper; those details are deferred to cited sources.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "... input into the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which computes normative z-scores ... relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18–100 (n = 6909), accounting for age, sex, intracranial volume, and image quality (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016)."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The NOMIS-based z-scores explicitly account for key covariates (age, sex, intracranial volume, image quality). Handling of potential multi-site or scanner effects in the reference cohort is not described here (would require details from the cited NOMIS references).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "... accounting for age, sex, intracranial volume, and image quality ... The normative values ... were derived from k-fold cross-validated regression models ..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the normative reference is specified by citing the NOMIS publications, giving the sample size and age range, and providing the repository URL for the scripts.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "... healthy adults ages 18–100 (n = 6909) ... (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016) ... via a freely available Python-based script (https://github.com/medicslab/NOMIS)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guidance, this item applies to PRIMARY data collection of the reference cohort. The study uses an EXISTING normative model (NOMIS) for the reference cohort; therefore, image acquisition protocol for the reference cohort is not applicable here.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "... input into the ... NOMIS software ... normative z-scores ... relative to a large sample of healthy adults ... (Potvin et al.)"

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is clearly described: T1-weighted images were segmented using FreeSurfer v6.0 recon-all, with visual QC following standardized SOPs before deriving NOMIS z-scores.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "All data passed visual quality control examination using standardized operating procedures ... Individual participant T1-weighted images were segmented using FreeSurfer v6.0 recon-all ... The aseg.stats file ... was then input into ... NOMIS ..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study does not build a NEW normative model; it uses an EXISTING model (NOMIS). Internal validation of the reference cohort pertains to model development and is not applicable here.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "... normative values ... were derived from k-fold cross-validated regression models ..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: An EXISTING normative model is used; application to an independent healthy dataset for external validation of a newly developed model does not apply.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Use of "NOMIS" reference values and scripts is cited rather than building a new model.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study did not develop a new normative model; it applied existing NOMIS-derived reference statistics. Detailed model type/settings are part of NOMIS and not described here.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "The normative values ... were derived from k-fold cross-validated regression models ... via a freely available Python-based script (https://github.com/medicslab/NOMIS)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Quantitative performance metrics for the reference model would be reported in the NOMIS sources. Since no NEW model was constructed here, this item is not applicable.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: No study-specific model performance reported; NOMIS is cited for reference values.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning of the reference cohort was performed by this study; it uses an EXISTING model. Partition characteristics therefore do not apply.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: Not applicable as no new model training/validation was conducted in this study.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and version for preprocessing are given (FreeSurfer v6.0; R 4.2.2 for stats). The source of the normative model is provided with citations and a GitHub URL to generate z-scores.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "... segmented using FreeSurfer v6.0 recon-all ..."; "... via a freely available Python-based script (https://github.com/medicslab/NOMIS)."; "Analyses were conducted in R (Version 4.2.2)."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Eligibility criteria are explicitly described (seeking treatment, DSM-5 CUD, age ≥18, recent use threshold) along with comprehensive exclusion criteria. Imaging QC and an exclusion for excessive head motion are specified, and the final sample size is reported.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Overall inclusion criteria ... seeking treatment for cannabis use, meet criteria for DSM-5 CUD, be at least 18 years old, and report cannabis use at least 3 days per week in the past month. Individuals were excluded ... [psychiatric, medical, pregnancy] ... Individuals were excluded from imaging procedures for ... One participant ... excluded ... for excessive head motion ... The final sample included 72 participants (50 males, 22 females)."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses included relevant clinical covariates: past-month cigarette smoking was included in all ANCOVAs; age of heaviest cannabis use onset was considered in sensitivity analyses; sex was included as an interaction term in GLMs relating z-scores to behaviors.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "Any reported past-month cigarette smoking was included as a covariate in all ANCOVA tests ... Follow-up sensitivity analyses including relevant demographic or behavioral variables ... were conducted ... GLMs with sex included as an interaction term ..."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: PRIMARY data collection is described as baseline data from two registered clinical trials at MUSC with NCT numbers and IRB approvals. Collection site is specified, but the time period of data collection is not stated.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The present study used pre-treatment baseline data from two clinical trials for CUD ... varenicline (n = 37; NCT02892110) ... TMS (n = 36; NCT03144232) ... Both trials were approved by the Medical University of South Carolina IRB ..."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample size is reported along with demographic characteristics (age distribution, race/ethnicity, marital status, education). Clinical characteristics are summarized and compared by sex, with specific measures included in Table 1.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "The final sample included 72 participants (50 males, 22 females)."; "Participants were 31 years old on average (SD = 9.8; range = 18–64), were predominantly non-Hispanic white (61%), unmarried (71%), and about half had at least some post-secondary education (53%). There were no sex differences in demographic characteristics (Table 1)."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Diagnostic criteria and several clinical measures are identified (DSM-5 CUD; Marijuana Craving Questionnaire subscales; Marijuana Problems Scale; Barratt Impulsiveness Scale). However, detailed assessment procedures are not elaborated beyond naming instruments and comparisons.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "... meet criteria for DSM-5 CUD ..."; Table 1 entries include "MCQ" subscales, "MJPS Total", and "BIS" scores.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The paper conveys the meaning of z-scores relative to a normative mean (z=0) and reports that average z-scores were within ±1.0 SD for both sexes. It interprets directionality in results (females generally higher thickness z-scores than males) and examines clinical associations. However, it does not define categorical thresholds for deviation (e.g., |Z|>1.96).
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "Average z-scores across all regions were well within ± 1.0 standard deviations of the normative z = 0 mean for both males and females."; "When normative modeling-derived z-scores are compared by sex, the results indicate differences in each group’s deviation from their age- and sex-matched peers; such scores provide insights into the potential clinical significance of observed deviations ..."
